sanity_expectations: k is strictly positive everywhere on the sampled grid
At fixed C_S, k increases monotonically with T (Arrhenius dominance)
At fixed T, k decreases with C_S at high C_S (product-inhibition and adsorption denominator dominate)
The diffusion factor (1+gamma_diff*sqrt(T/T_ref)*exp(-Ea_diff/(R*T))/(1+K_ads0*exp(-dH_ads/(R*T))*C_S))**(-1) < 1 and closer to 1 at high C_S (adsorption partially shields diffusion resistance)
k values span ~2 orders of magnitude across T=300-400 K
excitation_report: Dominant Arrhenius/adsorption term RMS ~70x sigma over the sampled (T,C_S) grid. New diffusion-limitation factor (1 + gamma_diff*sqrt(T/T_ref)*exp(-Ea_diff/(R*T))/(1+K_ads0*exp(-dH_ads/(R*T))*C_S))**(-1) reaches ~67x sigma (strongest at T~399 K, C_S~0.07 mol/L, where the diffusion resistance is largest relative to reaction rate). All terms visible above noise.

T: V->V (confirmed independent axis; upstream mislabeled as 'time axis')
C_S: V->V (confirmed independent axis; upstream mislabeled as 'time axis')
A: input->P (overridden: fixed pre-exponential parameter, not a sampling axis)
Ea: input->P (overridden: fixed activation-energy constant, not a sampling axis)
m, T_ref, K_ads0, dH_ads, C_S_ref, Theta_ref, f_deact, Ea_deact, K_prod0, dH_prod, beta_conv, gamma_diff, Ea_diff: P->P (all confirmed as fixed parameters)
rationale: Static explicit relation k = f(T, C_S; params). The upstream tag mistakenly labeled T, C_S, A, Ea as 'input/time axis'; structurally only T and C_S are independent axes of the k(T,C_S) surface (no derivatives or integrals). All remaining free symbols are fixed physical parameters. Ranges: T in [300,400] K covers a realistic catalytic window over which the Arrhenius factor spans ~2 orders of magnitude; C_S in [0.05,1.0] mol/L spans low-coverage to saturation regimes. Parameter magnitudes are chemically reasonable (Ea ~50 kJ/mol, exothermic adsorption enthalpies, mild deactivation). gamma_diff=100 sits at the upper edge of the suggested 1e-3–1e2 hint so the new diffusion-resistance factor produces visible curvature vs T at low C_S (~67 sigma), separating it from the parent kinetics/adsorption/deactivation/product-inhibition structure. 20x20 grid gives 400 samples.
